Erech
EE-rek
proper noun
Hebrew Erek, of uncertain meaning (some read “length”); one of the cities of the beginning of Nimrod’s kingdom in the land of Shinar, the Uruk of the plain.

📖 Biblical Definition

Erech stands second in the roll of Nimrod’s first cities: “And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar” (Gen 10:10). Here on the plain of Shinar, the same plain where men said, Go to, let us build us a city and a tower whose top may reach unto heaven, rose the first empire of the world. Nimrod was a mighty hunter before the LORD, and the beginning of his kingdom was Babel and her sister cities. Erech was thus a stone in the first monument of man’s self-exaltation, the kingdom of the earth set up over against the kingdom of God. Yet even this the LORD ruled and overruled, for He made of one blood all nations of men to dwell on all the face of the earth, and determined the times before appointed and the bounds of their habitation (Act 17:26). The heathen rage and the people imagine a vain thing (Psa 2:1); the towers of Shinar rise and fall; but the counsel of the LORD standeth for ever. And out of these scattered nations He drew forth Abram, and promised, In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed (Gen 12:3). Erech built for man’s glory; God builds a city for His own, and the gates of Babel shall not prevail against it.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

One of the first cities of Nimrod’s kingdom in the land of Shinar (Gen 10:10); a stone in the first empire of man’s self-exaltation, ruled and overruled by the sovereign LORD.

expand to see more

ERECH, a city of Shinar, second named in Nimrod’s kingdom.

Founded on the plain where Babel’s tower was built.

A monument of man’s dominion set over against the kingdom of God.

Yet the LORD appointed the times and bounds of every people (Act 17:26).

The heathen rage, but the counsel of the LORD standeth for ever.

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 10:10 — "And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar."

Psa 2:1 — "Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing?"

Act 17:26 — "And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;"

Gen 12:3 — "And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A city of Nimrod’s kingdom in Shinar; it recovers the sovereignty of God over the empires of man and the vanity of the tower-builder’s pride.

expand to see more

Erech is an ancient name in a genealogy of nations, and the world raises no quarrel over a ruin on the plain of Shinar. Its lesson is written plain in the text: the first kingdom of the earth began in rebellion, and the first empire was Babel.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the sovereignty of God over the kingdoms of men. Nimrod built for his own name, and the towers of Shinar rose in pride; but the LORD made of one blood all nations and set the times and bounds of their habitation. The heathen rage and imagine a vain thing, yet the counsel of the LORD standeth for ever, and out of the scattered peoples He called Abram, that in his Seed all families of the earth should be blessed.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Erek, of uncertain sense; a city of the land of Shinar and one of the first seats of Nimrod’s kingdom.

expand to see more

Erech — a city of Shinar in Nimrod’s kingdom (Gen 10:10).

Hebrew Erek, meaning uncertain, sometimes read “length.”

The Uruk of the southern plain, near Babel.

Named second among Babel, Accad, and Calneh.

A seat of the first empire raised on the plain of rebellion.

Usage

"Erech was among the first cities of Nimrod’s kingdom."

"It lay in the land of Shinar, near Babel."

"The name Erech stands second in the roll of Genesis ten."
